findings.title: create ignores alias_level
findings.body: The client sends `alias_level` in `asJSON` when creating a group, but `create` never assigns `params[:alias_level]`. Any alias level chosen when creating a new group is silently dropped and the group gets the default.

findings.title: totalPages off by one when count is a multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` is computed as `floor(user_count/limit)+1`, so 50 members with a limit of 50 shows 2 pages. Because `showingLast` compares `currentPage` with this inflated total, the next button stays enabled on the last real page. Clicking it sets offset to `user_count` and fetches an empty member list. Use `Math.ceil(user_count/limit)`.

findings.title: Unbounded limit on public members endpoint
findings.body: The public `members` endpoint takes `limit` straight from the request with no maximum. Any user can request e.g. `limit=1000000` on a large automatic group and force a huge query and serialization. Negative `limit`/`offset` values are not rejected either. Clamp both values to a sane range.

findings.title: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise
findings.body: When the group name is empty, `findMembers` now returns `undefined` instead of a resolved promise. The `next`/`previous` actions return its result, so any caller that chains `.then()` on it will throw.

findings.title: `automatic` not resolved in item view context
findings.body: Inside the `each ... itemView` the template context is the item view, so `automatic` likely does not resolve to the group's property. The remove link may then be shown for automatic groups; the server rejects the request with a 422, so the user sees a broken action.

findings.title: remove_member bypasses group.remove
findings.body: `remove_member` calls `group.users.delete(user_id)` with a raw id instead of the existing `group.remove(user)` API used elsewhere. Removing by integer id on a has_many through association is unreliable, and any callbacks or side effects in `group.remove` are skipped.

findings.title: Test uses wrong HTTP verb
findings.body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" sends `xhr :put` to `remove_member`, but the route is DELETE. It therefore does not exercise the real routed request.

findings.title: addMembers has no error handling and doesn't clear input
findings.body: `addMembers` has no failure handler, so failed additions (e.g. the 422 for automatic groups) fail silently with no message to the admin. The username input is also never cleared after a successful add (noted by the TODO), so it can be resubmitted by accident.
